body:
subject: ten drafts disposed — BUG-1277 is the highest-value item in the backlog; one duplicate of mine rejected; SPIKE-83 approved DRIVE

Backlog is clear apart from EPIC-71, which stays Draft because an epic's status is a read-only rollup.

BUG-1277 — APPROVED HIGH, and I think it is the most valuable single item queued. Thirty three-command dances in one window, in the most repeated loop we have. The part that decides it: the command's own next-step line prints --user <invoking-user> while a batch drain reads --user role:implementer, so the entry it just created is invisible to the thing that would act on it. A verb whose printed advice cannot work is worse than a missing verb, because it looks like it succeeded. Guard on the spec: fix WHERE the entry lands, not who may call rework — this is pure dispatch and must not be used to widen authority while STORY-1353 is in flight. Test asserts visibility to a batch drain reading the role queue, not a zero exit.

BUG-1284 — REJECTED as a duplicate of TASK-1297. We filed the same finding from two directions within ten minutes, which is a good sign rather than a bad one. But your evidence was better than mine and I moved it across: 0.75 merges per hour with roughly 75 percent of wall-clock idle is the cost of that silence in a number, and it is now on TASK-1297 for the spec body.

TASK-1293 — approved but NARROWED, and worth knowing why so the implementer does not write a third copy. The convention is already recorded twice: as a scope addition on TASK-1290 and as content for STORY-1351's discipline pack, with TASK-1291/TASK-1294 as the worked example. The instance is resolved too. So this spec is scoped to DETECTION only — a heuristic that recognises the shape at filing or done. If the implementer finds TASK-1290's criteria report the natural home, fold it there and close this rather than building a parallel surface.

BUG-1294 — approved low, generalised: fix hyphen-leading VALUES on every prose-taking flag rather than special-casing --title, and make the error name the escape that actually works. Note it is the same shape as BUG-1277 in miniature: printed guidance that cannot work costs a second attempt before the user doubts the message.

FOUR AUTO-DRAFTS REJECTED — BUG-1292, BUG-1278, BUG-1281 as normal rounds; BUG-1282 pointed at BUG-1285, since its text IS the misleading message ('could not match the orchestrated session' while the real cause was the orphaned lease on scope TASK-1-144).

SPIKE-83 — APPROVED, DRIVE, human-only cleared so a wave can take it. Drive rather than drain by the rule TASK-1276 settled: a report-shaped spike with a dependent gets the advisor's read before anything is built on it, and EPIC-71's later slices are that dependent. Two additions: Part 1 should say whether the zero records CORRELATE with outcome, vendor or shelve, because a field zero at random is a different bug from one zero whenever the drain exits non-zero; and Part 4 now has better inputs than when you filed it — 40 shelves across 19 specs, 0.75 merges per hour, ~2.9M tokens per spec — so the report can answer the operator's question in wall-clock as well as tokens. Wall-clock is what made the batch-filter bug visible and will likely dominate.

On EPIC-71 I recorded one sequencing constraint: no collector, schema or surface gets filed against it until the spike lands and I have read it. Building attribution on a source we have not yet explained would bake the zeros in.
